title: Seat three boxes in keyed rail bays
instruction: Seat the three orange boxes in the three rail bays, one per bay, each flat between its rails with one end within 5 mm of the end stop.
context: A 1 g bench analogue of spacecraft integration: avionics boxes are set onto a bracket plate whose keyed footprints run at odd angles, and a box set down across its rails does not seat. The test is orientation matching to three different keys, including an oblique one, with 3 mm of channel clearance and 5 mm of end registration. It is a fit-up test, not a reach test, and it claims nothing about microgravity.
setup: On the table in front of the left arm (x forward from the arm bases, y left; the left arm's base is 305 mm left of the midline). Fixed, grey (sRGB 0.5, 0.5, 0.5), matte, 12 mm tall, standing on the table: three rail bays, each two rails 76 x 8 mm with their inner faces 41 mm apart and one end stop 8 x 41 mm. Each rail is centred abeam its bay centre and runs 38 mm either way along the bay axis; the stop fits between the rails at the stop end with its inner face 37 mm from the bay centre, so it overlaps the rail ends by 1 mm and stands 7 mm past them, and every pocket is 75 mm long and 41 mm wide. Bay A, rails running forward, centred 180 mm in front of the base line and 165 mm inboard of the left arm's base, stop at the far end. Bay B, rails running across the table, centred 180 mm in front and 35 mm inboard, stop at the outboard end. Bay C, rails running at 45 degrees toward forward and outboard, centred 180 mm in front and 95 mm outboard, stop at the forward-outboard end. In table coordinates (metres; x forward, y left, origin on the base line at the midline) the bay centres are (0.180, 0.140), (0.180, 0.270) and (0.180, 0.400), each rail's centre is 24.5 mm either side of its bay axis and each stop's centre is 41 mm from its bay centre along the rails. Loose, orange (sRGB 0.9, 0.45, 0.1), matte: three identical boxes 70 mm long, 35 mm wide and 45 mm tall, 100 g each, standing on a 70 x 35 face with the long axis forward, centred 330 mm in front of the base line at 165 mm inboard, 35 mm inboard and 95 mm outboard of the left arm's base, each 150 mm beyond its bay's centre and at least 68 mm clear of every rail and stop. A box fits a pocket with 3 mm of clearance per side and a 2 mm end gap when centred. The boxes are 95 mm apart edge to edge, and neighbouring bays at least 38 mm apart (bay B's stop to bay C's nearest rail). The right arm is idle at its ready pose. To build it: cut the rails and stops from 8 x 12 mm strip (wood, acrylic or printed), glue them to a board taped to the table at the stated centres, and print or cut the boxes from wood to 100 g.
scoring: End state only, judged per bay from a photo and a tape measure. A box is seated in a bay when it rests flat on the table between that bay's rails (bottom within 4 mm of the table, tilt under 5 degrees with either 70 x 35 face down, long axis within 7 degrees of the rail direction either way round, centre within 4 mm of the bay axis, at rest under 10 mm/s) with its end face 0 to 5 mm from the stop's inner face. A box is channelled when it passes the same tests but its end face is 5 to 25 mm from the stop. Each bay scores once, at its best box: seated 1/3, channelled 1/6, otherwise 0; the task score is the sum over the three bays, so 0, 0.17, 0.33, 0.5, 0.67, 0.83 or 1.0. Any box may go to any bay. A box resting on a rail or stop, lying across a bay, tilted, lifted, moving, behind a stop, off the table or anywhere else earns nothing, and a second box in a bay adds nothing. Success, which ends the trial, is all three bays seated and still for 1 s. In simulation the horizontal tests use the box centre and its quaternion, not the axis-aligned bounds, so the 45 degree bay is judged correctly; the bottom height is the box's lowest point; an exact 5.0 mm gap counts as seated (0.1 mm epsilon) and up to 2 mm of solver penetration into the stop counts as touching. The rails and stops are fixed in simulation; on the real rig, a trial in which any rail or stop moves more than 5 mm from its mark scores 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the three boxes back on their marks, long axis forward; the rails and stops do not move.
fidelity: Approximate: rigid boxes and rails sharing one matte material (friction 1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic); no fasteners, connectors, thermal interface or harness; the fixtures cannot move; the oblique bay stands in for the odd mounting angles of real bracket plates; Earth gravity on a bench, which is also where this job is done. The one tolerance that matters, 3 mm of rail clearance per side, is reproduced exactly.
